doctrine: Digital products are the highest-leverage solo operator model: build once, sell infinitely, near-zero marginal cost. AI collapsed production barriers (outline to final PDF in days). Distribution is the business, not the product. Core thesis: niche validation before build (Amazon/Medium/Reddit review mining), micro-niche targeting ("knee pain for marathoners over 50" beats "fitness"), product ladder architecture ($0 lead magnet → $7-27 PDF → $27-97 manual → $97-497 video course → $500-5000+ coaching → $1000-20000+ done-for-you). Each rung qualifies buyers for the next. Ownership via email list (sole platform-independent asset). Production: structure via AI outline, draft chapter-by-chapter (not all at once), inject voice/examples, design in Canva, PAS sales copy. Platform selection: Gumroad/KDP for first product (speed to market), migrate to Payhip/Stan Store/Shopify when revenue justifies control. Traffic stacking: search-based (Medium, Pinterest, YouTube, Amazon SEO) compounds; social decays. SEO-optimized articles, specific titles, evergreen pins. AI services model: don't sell AI, sell outcomes (e.g., "24/7 appointment booking system" not "chatbot implementation"). Lego-brick approach: build one module for one client, package for 50 in the niche, $500-2000/month retainer, 90%+ margins. Operator timeline: Week 1 niche validation (3 questions: what do people ask you, what you solved, what's easy for you), Week 2 MVP + storefront, Week 3 lead magnet + traffic, Week 4+ email list, Month 2-3 next rung, Month 3-6 service layer, Month 6+ autopilot. Utility beats aesthetics. Third Layer Theory: deep specialization = low competition, high conversion. Competitor gap analysis (1-2 star reviews) is your roadmap.

Niche validation: Amazon search/review audit, Medium 3-article test, Reddit/Facebook group signal hunt

AI production pipeline: outline (prompt-driven structure), chapter-by-chapter draft (quality degrades on long outputs), voice injection (experience + examples + opinions), design in Canva, PAS copy for sales page
Product ladder progression: lead magnet ($0) → low-ticket PDF ($7-27) → mid-ticket manual ($27-97) → video course ($97-497) → coaching ($500-5000+) → done-for-you ($1000-20000+)
Traffic stacking (compounding): Medium (weekly SEO articles) + Pinterest (evergreen pins) + YouTube (linked content) + Amazon SEO (specific titles) → owned email list as conversion layer
AI service play: outcome definition → single-module MVP → one-client proof → package for 50 same-niche clients → $500-2000/month retainer

Operator timeline: Week 1 niche + validation, Week 2 MVP + launch, Week 3 lead magnet setup, Weeks 3-4 traffic channel pick + content, ongoing email growth, Month 2-3 next product tier, Month 3-6 service layer, Month 6+ automation + compounding
prompts: What do people already come to me for advice on? (product discovery)
What problems have I solved for myself? (transformation as product)
What comes easily to me but is hard for others? (latent skill monetization)
Create a 10-chapter outline for an ebook that teaches [specific audience] how to [specific outcome] (AI production structure)
Search [topic] on Amazon and extract 1-2 star review complaints for roadmap (validation via gap analysis)
tools: Amazon KDP (print-on-demand, built-in discovery, lower royalty tradeoff)
Gumroad (simple digital products, 10% fees, faster to market than alternatives)
Medium (SEO-ranked content, compounding passive traffic, product link embeds)
Pinterest (evergreen search engine, pin creation tools, long-tail traffic)
YouTube (compounding video search, suggested content, description CTAs)
Canva (template-based design, no design skills required)
Payhip (branding control, lower fees, no built-in discovery)
Stan Store (link-in-bio, mobile-first, creator-focused, subscription cost)
Shopify (full control, custom storefront, overkill for first product)
AI models (outline, draft, sales copy generation: structure-first, chapter-by-chapter to avoid degradation)
operating_rules: Build once, sell infinitely (digital product core thesis)
Distribution is the business, not the product (traffic/conversion/list > asset quality)
Utility beats aesthetics (specific problem solver > pretty/comprehensive)
Niche depth > breadth (micro-niche = low competition, high conversion)
Validate before build (Amazon/Medium/Reddit signal hunt mandatory)
Rule of One applies (one product, one person, one page, one traffic channel per launch)
Email list is sole platform-independent asset (own the distribution)
Each product rung qualifies for next (trust-building funnel, not cold sales at each tier)
AI production: chapter-by-chapter not all-at-once (long outputs degrade quality)
Voice injection mandatory (raw AI output reads generic, separates $5 from $47 products)
Search channels compound, social decays (prioritize SEO-based over short-form)
Specific titles win ("AI Prompts for Real Estate Agents" > "The Future of Property Marketing")
Don't sell AI, sell outcomes ("24/7 appointment booking" not "chatbot implementation")
Lego-brick agency model (one module for one client, then scale to 50 in niche)
90%+ margin on AI services (AI tools cost near-zero, client pays for outcome/management)
